description:
FOUND s505 (Fable, 2026-10-03) by a review probe of s501t (#155 tie): core Tie::File now ties and reads correctly, but `$l[1] = "CHANGED"` writes the record WITHOUT its record separator -- the file reads `l1|CHANGEDl3|l4` where perl writes `l1|CHANGED|l3|l4`.  Silent corruption of a file on disk.

CAUSE (probed perl -> main a33ce274 -> a0899ba6; identical on both PCL trees, so PRE-EXISTING and not tie): Tie::File::STORE does `my ($self, $n, $rec) = @_; $self->_fixrecs($rec);` and _fixrecs appends the separator THROUGH @_ (`my $self = shift; for (@_) { $_ .= $self->{recsep} unless ... }`).  A plain `my` lexical of a SUB passed to a callee the compiler cannot see -- a METHOD call, a package-QUALIFIED call (`T::m2($self, $rec)`), a dynamic method, a coderef call -- is passed as a COPY, so the write is lost.  That is the documented partial in docs/not-supported.md "@_ argument aliasing -- PARTIAL" (what still COPIES: coderef calls, method dispatch, cross-file callees).

TWO THINGS THAT ENTRY DOES NOT SAY:
(1) THE BACKSTOP IS SILENT HERE.  The entry promises the runtime warning "Cannot modify non-boxed value" as the loud backstop "for exactly these".  ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/min/f4c.pl prints NOTHING on stderr while seven of its ten rows are wrong (`$_ .= "x"` in a foreach over @_, `$_[1] .= "x"`): the callee receives a fresh BOX holding the copy, so the write succeeds -- into the copy.  The warning only fires for a RAW value.  So this is a silent wrong, not an announced one.
(2) A QUALIFIED call to a sub IN THE SAME FILE (`T::m2($self, $rec)`) copies too, although the callee body is visible -- writes_args is consulted by bare name only.

Reproducers: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/min/f4.pl, f4b.pl (which callee shapes: only the parameter-of-a-sub + unseen-callee combination fails; a FILE-level `my` is right, an ARRAY parameter is right, a parameter that is also read by another statement form (`chomp(my $c = $rec)`) is right), f4c.pl (ten caller shapes; perl: all `vx`), and the module row: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/r501t-mods.pl row 13.

WHAT TO MEASURE BEFORE DESIGNING (this is the E2c / #189 / #862 territory -- read DECIDED for writes_args first): how many call sites in the corpus pass a raw-slot `my` scalar to a method / qualified / coderef call (one counter in VarAnnotator at the arg-to-writer decision), and what boxing ALL of them costs on tools/bench-exec.pl rows methret / sigarith / passarr.  Cheaper candidates, in order: (a) resolve a package-QUALIFIED same-file callee through the existing writes_args fact (finding 2 -- no cost); (b) a file-level fact "some sub in this compilation unit writes @_ and is reachable as a method" boxing only arguments of method calls whose NAME matches such a sub (same-file methods; Tie::File is one file); (c) cross-file: the fact rides the module cache manifest.  The USER rule applies: a correctness fix that slows the generated code is flagged with its number.

Until fixed: add Tie::File to the not-supported entry affected list (real module, silent file corruption), and say there that the backstop does not fire for these shapes.


=== DESIGN (s517, Fable, 2026-10-15; RULED into s517b, which #3161 zlib is BLOCKED on: Compress::Zlib::compress does `my $output; $x->deflate($in, $output)` -- a METHOD call across files -- and returns "" SILENTLY under the shim) ===
THE SETTLED CONSTRAINTS (DECIDED, read before touching anything): #189 -- "NO blanket boxing of call args, ever"; writes_args is a CALLEE-body fact consumed as the `arg-to-writer` boxing reason at same-file call sites; the runtime warning was meant as the backstop for method / coderef / cross-file callees and this task shows it is SILENT (the callee gets a fresh box).  #3060 = the NAMED cross-file half (imported / package-qualified callee: carry writes_args in the module-cache record) -- it cannot reach a METHOD call, whose callee is resolved at run time (IO::Compress::Base->compr lands in an adapter class Base never `use`s), so a name-keyed fact, same-file or manifest, does not close this task.
THE SHAPE THAT DOES, keeping #189: COPY-IN / COPY-OUT AT THE CALL SITE, for a raw-slot `my` SCALAR argument of an UNSEEN callee (method call, coderef call `&$c(...)` / `$c->(...)`, a qualified or bare call whose callee record is absent).  The caller's variable STAYS RAW (no boxing of the variable, the raw-slot lever is kept); the argument is passed in a fresh box held by the CALLER, and after the call the caller stores the box's value back into the slot:
    (let ((#:b1 (make-pl-box $x)))                       ; one box per raw-slot scalar arg, made in the caller
      (multiple-value-prog1 (p-method-call $obj "m" (vector #:b1 ...))   ; the callee writes $_[N] into #:b1 as it does today
        (setq $x (p-box-value #:b1))))                    ; the write reaches the slot
Hold the BOXES, never the vector indices: the callee's `shift` moves the elements, the box identity does not.  ONE helper in the lowering, used by every unseen-callee call shape (rule 11) -- the same place that decides "this callee is unseen" today; `PCL_OPT=none` has no raw slots, so it emits nothing new and must RUN identically.  A variable passed this way is EXCLUDED from the raw-NUMERIC verdict (stays raw-UNTYPED): a string written back into a typed slot must be impossible by construction (rule 12), never a run-time type error -- check how the verdict treats a call argument today and write it down.  The INVOCANT (`$_[0]` of a method call) is included in the counter and the A/B and ships if it is inside the band (perl aliases it too).
WHAT IT DOES NOT GIVE (write into not-supported with a probe each, under the aliasing section): a callee that RETAINS `\$_[N]` and writes after returning; the same variable passed twice to one call (two boxes, the last read-back wins); a callee that reads the caller's variable through a closure WHILE writing `$_[N]` (sees the pre-call value); a die inside the callee after a partial write (no unwind-protect in the first build: the read-back is skipped, the caller keeps the pre-call value -- measure the cost of unwind-protect only if the band allows it).
MEASURE FIRST (the task's own order): (1) the counter at the arg-to-writer decision over the four populations -- call sites that pass a raw-slot `my` scalar to an unseen callee, by shape (method / coderef / qualified / bare), and how many distinct variables; (2) `tools/bench-exec.pl` base / tree / base on methret, sigarith, passarr, fibret, subret, gcdret, the control band, and any row the counter says is dense.  SHIP if the OO rows hold the band or the cost is small and NAMED (the USER rule: a correctness fix that slows generated code is FLAGGED with its number, never hidden); if the cost is large, FILE the numbers, keep the shim committed and unshipped, report NOT MERGE-READY on the zlib acceptance -- the USER decides perf vs correctness.
BAR: Tie::File `$l[1] = "x"` round trip = perl (this task's victim); f4c.pl's ten shapes (`~/pcl-agent-scratch/s505/review/min/f4c.pl`); #3060's repro (`WA::app($s)`) = perl -- the same mechanism closes its symptom, #3060's manifest route becomes the EXACT refinement for named callees and stays filed; Compress::Zlib compress / uncompress / IO::Compress round trips = perl; the guard rows FAIL on main; corpus-diff every file explained by the verdict (many); emission-ab RCDIFF 0; ir-conform; the sweep; the board; everyday; gen v2-6484.
subject: A sub parameter (`my` scalar) passed to a METHOD / qualified / coderef call is COPIED, so the callee`s write through @_ is lost SILENTLY (the documented @_-aliasing partial; its "loud backstop" does not fire): core Tie::File STORE drops the record separator -- `$l[1] = "x"` corrupts the file
